title: SslHandler#unwrap must send fireChannelRead event after a notification for a handshake success

timeline.body:
Motivation:

In some use cases `SslHandler#unwrap` sends `fireChannelRead` event before a notification for a handshake success.
Such use case is a HTTP server that supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 via `ApplicationProtocolNegotiationHandler`,
in this case `fireChannelRead` is sent before `ApplicationProtocolNegotiationHandler` is able to setup properly the pipeline
depending on the negotiated protocol. The issue is visible when `SslProvider.OPENSSL` is configured.
This is a regression caused by #11156

Modifications:

- SslHandler#unwrap sends fireChannelRead event after a notification for a handshake success
- Add test

Result:

Fixes #11201

reply.body: Sorry I missed that with the initial commit

timeline.body: The test timeout will not be able to unblock the test thread when we use `syncUninterruptibly` here…

reply.body:
Interesting
Do you mean that the exception will not be thrown or that the thread will not be interrupted?

https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/d22a35628db9b9bd473d7be76d989b05fdc7a12f/common/src/main/java/io/netty/util/concurrent/DefaultPromise.java#L262-L290

```
org.junit.runners.model.TestTimedOutException: test timed out after 5000 milliseconds

	at java.lang.Object.wait(Native Method)
	at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:502)
	at io.netty.util.concurrent.DefaultPromise.awaitUninterruptibly(DefaultPromise.java:275)
	at io.netty.channel.DefaultChannelPromise.awaitUninterruptibly(DefaultChannelPromise.java:137)
	at io.netty.channel.DefaultChannelPromise.awaitUninterruptibly(DefaultChannelPromise.java:30)
	at io.netty.util.concurrent.DefaultPromise.syncUninterruptibly(DefaultPromise.java:411)
	at io.netty.channel.DefaultChannelPromise.syncUninterruptibly(DefaultChannelPromise.java:125)
	at io.netty.channel.DefaultChannelPromise.syncUninterruptibly(DefaultChannelPromise.java:30)
	at io.netty.handler.codec.http2.Http2MultiplexTransportTest.testFireChannelReadAfterHandshakeSuccess(Http2MultiplexTransportTest.java:567)
```
I think he means that the thread will not be interrupted.

timeline.body: this may result in data being dropped, which is observed in `SocketSslEchoTest`. I ran your tests against https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/11210 and this seems to fix the issue. can you verify https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/11210 fixes the root cause? if so I propose we merge https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/11210, then merge the unit tests from this PR.

reply.body: @Scottmitch Thanks a lot, with #11210 I do not see the issue anymore!
@violetagg I just merged #11210 ... Can you please revert the change in this class and rebase ? This way we can pull in your unit test and also verify it passes on the CI.
